game.title: XIII
game.build_notes: Verified against the Steam 'XIII - Classic' build on Windows 10, 2026-08-27. The engine build is ANSI, not Unicode — console commands pass as plain char*.

api_notes: This game does not need synthetic input for most automation: it has a real console and an internal command dispatcher that can be driven directly (see `commands`).
A native console exists on F2.

Synthetic keyboard input works: `keybd_event` with the virtual-key code, sent to the FOREGROUND window, drives menus (Enter/Escape/arrows), movement (W/A/S/D), turning (U/J, bound to TurnLeft/TurnRight: a 120 ms hold is about 20 degrees, 300 ms about 45) and numpad hotkeys (verified live 2026-09-11). Send numpad keys by virtual-key code; a scancode-only send becomes Home/arrows when NumLock is off.

bindings.notes: From a community wiki. The command set it exposes has since been verified directly (see `commands`), but the F2 binding itself was not exercised — commands were issued programmatically instead.

detect.cue: the camera-view function is being called each frame; camera position updates

states.description: Any menu, including the save menu.

detect.cue: the per-frame camera-view function STOPS being called — position telemetry goes silent

states.notes: Useful and slightly counter-intuitive: the absence of telemetry is itself the state signal. A queued command will sit unconsumed until gameplay resumes.

dispatch_notes: Commands resolve against DIFFERENT objects, and this is the single most useful fact in this profile. Sending a cheat to the wrong one silently returns 'unhandled'.

Player-owned commands resolve on APlayerController. Cheats resolve on UCheatManager, which the console reaches by hopping from the controller — calling the controller alone finds only its own commands.
Engine-level commands (open, start) resolve on the game engine object.
IMPORTANT: dispatch must happen in the GAME-LOGIC phase. Executing a console command from a render-path hook caused an immediate general protection fault — see UNIVERSAL.md.

available.name: Fly
available.effect: free flight, gravity off, collision kept

available.name: HealMe <n>
available.notes: Observed raising health 50 -> 100 in game — the end-to-end proof that external command injection worked.

absent.notes: All standard Unreal Engine 2 commands, all returning unhandled on both the controller and the cheat manager in this build. 'It is a standard UE2 command, therefore it is here' does NOT hold. Teleport's absence is the most limiting — there is no console-driven way to reposition the player.

entry_points.notes: Level codes exist for this engine but were not catalogued for this game.

routes.how: Run `XIII.exe Plage01` with the working directory set to `system\`. Any map name works the same way (standard Unreal Engine 2 command line).
routes.lands_in: Plage01 (the first level with free control), after a short in-engine cutscene
routes.notes: No Steam round-trip happened: the process that started is the game itself, and XIII.log shows `Browse: Plage01`. `-windowed` is not a switch this game parses; windowed mode comes from the ini.

routes.how: `steam://rungameid/1170760`, wait for the profile screen (intro videos end by themselves in about 20 s), then Enter x3: the pre-selected profile, then Continue, then PLAY. Space dismisses the objectives card.
routes.lands_in: the profile's last checkpoint (Banque01 on the dev PC, 2026-09-11)
routes.notes: On the profile screen Up wraps to 'Create new profile'; Escape backs out of it. The menu cursor does not follow Windows mouse clicks, so drive menus with the keyboard.

hazards.description: The main loop polls the foreground window every iteration and stops ticking the engine when the game is not foreground.
hazards.impact: Any automation waiting on the game to advance stalls the moment focus is lost — including when the operator alt-tabs to type.
hazards.mitigation: Redirect the game's own foreground query so it always sees its own window.

hazards.description: Command dispatch runs from the per-frame player tick, which does not run while a menu is open.
hazards.impact: A queued command sits unexecuted, which can look like the harness being broken.

hazards.description: The external command queue (`xiii_automation_cmds.txt`) and camera telemetry exist only in the 0.2.8/0.2.9 graphics-proxy builds. The M2 stereo builds have neither, and no focus fix either.
hazards.impact: With a stereo build installed, commands in the queue file are ignored and the engine stops ticking whenever the window loses focus.
hazards.mitigation: Drive stereo builds with keyboard input to the foreground window and start levels from the command line. Before re-activating 0.2.9, empty the queue file and set `[VR] AutomationEngineExec=0`: two stale engine-tier lines left in it would replay the known crash on the first gameplay tick.
hazards.confidence_notes: The harness strings are absent from the stereo builds' binaries (measured). The crash replay is read from code, not reproduced.

hazards.description: All verified work on this build was done windowed. A fullscreen device re-acquire crashed the game while a graphics proxy was loaded.
hazards.impact: Unclear whether fullscreen is genuinely unsafe — the crash was later traced to a different cause — but windowed is the only configuration with a track record here.
